generation.result_format: documented expected rows; not external execution

basis: Expected rows are pinned to the documented SQL semantics linked below; external engines are not executed by this fixture test. WITH TIES cases follow PostgreSQL 16 (DuckDB 1.5.5 does not implement WITH TIES); plain LIMIT/OFFSET/FETCH cases agree between both engines. Setup: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, score INTEGER); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1,10),(2,20),(3,20),(4,20),(5,30),(6,NULL).

cases.name: offset_rows_then_fetch_next_only
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY id OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY

cases.name: with_ties_keeps_boundary_peers
cases.sql: SELECT id, score FROM t ORDER BY score FETCH FIRST 2 ROWS WITH TIES

cases.name: with_ties_multi_key_breaks_the_tie
cases.sql: SELECT id, score FROM t ORDER BY score DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC FETCH FIRST 2 ROWS WITH TIES

cases.name: with_ties_null_boundary_is_its_own_peer_group
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY score NULLS FIRST FETCH FIRST 1 ROW WITH TIES

cases.name: with_ties_after_offset_does_not_revive_discarded_rows
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY score OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH FIRST 1 ROW WITH TIES

cases.name: limit_null_and_offset_null_mean_no_bound
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT NULL OFFSET NULL

cases.name: constant_expression_counts_fold_at_plan_time
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM t ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 + 1 OFFSET 10 / 2
